title: Review: jmap-mail-server RFC 8621 handlers
description: Code review of all work done on jmap-mail-server (RFC 8621 handler layer). Covers correctness, maintainer risk, efficiency, and Rust idioms.
notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — five P0 correctness bugs including silent spec non-conformance (onSuccessUpdateOriginal missing, wrong call_id format), a missing validation (empty mailboxIds), an update restriction bypass (undoStatus-only not enforced), and a within-request ordering bug (create+destroy child mailbox).
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — no unsafe, no Box<dyn Error> in public API, ownership patterns are reasonable. Main smell is the v.clone() pattern repeated for every serde parse and the duplicated Display/serde camelCase strings in SetErrorType.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: JMAP-9gp.9 (VacationResponse TOCTOU — depends on whether MailBackend implementations provide their own locking). Uncertainty driven by: no read of the common/mod.rs MemoryBackend implementation for find_thread_by_message_ids, and no read of jmap_types::JmapError API. Would raise confidence if: ran cargo test, verified RFC 8620 §6.3 onSuccessUpdateOriginal wire format.
